title: fix(route.cli): ignore EPIPE when stdout closes early, so a pipe into head cannot crash a recorded act
description:
## what

the route cli (`rhx route.*`) crashes with a node stack when its stdout closes early, e.g. `rhx route.stone.set … | head -n 1`.

## why

`head -n 1` closes the pipe after one line; the next `console.log` in `rhachet-roles-bhrain/dist/contract/cli/route.js:1076` hits `write EPIPE`, an unhandled `'error'` event on the stdout socket, so node exits nonzero with `💥 failed with an error`.

the caller cannot tell a recorded act from a lost one. a re-run with `| tail -2` printed `🦉 absorbed:` for each slug, so the act is idempotent and was recorded — but the crash output does not say so.

## evidence

seen seven times in a row in `ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-ehmpathy`, route `v2026_09_26.fix-blocklist-nudge`, stone 5.1, on `rhx route.stone.set --stone <s> --as absorbed --that <slug> | head -n 1`.

## shape

in the cli entry, ignore EPIPE on stdout and stderr — the node equivalent of the `trap '' PIPE` the ehmpathy hooks use:

```ts
process.stdout.on('error', (e) => { if (e.code === 'EPIPE') process.exit(0); throw e; });
```

clamp: spawn the cli piped into a reader that closes after one line; assert exit 0 and that the act recorded.
